Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a reticular interstitial pattern with prominent linear markings, particularly in the upper and mid-lung zones, which is characteristic of the subpleural cysts and interstitial thickening seen in Down syndrome-associated lung disease. This distribution (upper lobe predominance) and associated linear thickening distinguish it from other cystic lung diseases that typically favor the lower lobes.
